headline: Majors rally hard on the week and month but sold into today, positioning crowded and expensive, whales flowing onto exchanges for three straight weeks.
paragraphs: Every major asset trades above its 200-day moving average, and every one has MACD above signal, which means the intermediate trend is up and momentum is synchronized with it. Bitcoin sits 38 percent below its 12-month high, Ethereum 48.5 percent below, and the broader names even deeper in their draws, yet the tape over the last seven and thirty days reads unmistakably bullish. Bitcoin is up 19.6 percent on the week and 21.2 percent on the month, while Ethereum has climbed 26.6 percent and 30.2 percent in the same windows. Solana's story is more violent: up 34.7 percent on the week and 37.8 percent on the month, and XRP is up 37.9 percent on the week. These are not resting rallies; they are acceleration rallies. The contradiction is the next point: all seven majors are down on the day, ranging from Bitcoin at minus 3.6 percent to Cardano at minus 5.5 percent. This is a pullback inside an uptrend, and it arrived as Fear and Greed sits at 68, in the greed zone, after ranging between 25 and 74 over the last thirty days. The crowd is confident, prices are elevated relative to the longer trend, and today the tape is selling.

Momentum readings expose the tension. Bitcoin's RSI-14 is 68.9 and Ethereum's is 68.6, both firmly in overbought territory, yet neither has triggered a golden cross (the 50-day above the 200-day), a condition that would normally suggest the move is mature and due for a rest. Solana's RSI is even hotter at 73.7. RSI above 70 in a bull move can signal strength or exhaustion depending on the next bar; this one is being tested today. Cardano and Dogecoin present a different picture: Cardano's RSI sits at 53.3, neutral, and it trades below its 200-day despite rallying 15.9 percent on the week and 25.8 percent on the month, which is a divergence between momentum (the week and month gains) and regime (below the long-term average). Dogecoin also sits below its 200-day despite 20.9 percent weekly and 17.4 percent monthly gains. These two are running against the structural current, a sign that their rallies may be more speculative than structural.

Leverage positioning reveals crowding and cost. Bitcoin's funding rate at OKX stands at 0.44 basis points per eight hours, or 4.8 percent annualized, which is elevated; traders are paying to hold longs. Ethereum's funding is even steeper at 0.01 percent per eight hours, or 11 percent annualized, among the highest costs on the board. Solana is the outlier, with negative funding at minus 0.0011 percent per eight hours, meaning shorts are paying longs, yet Solana's long-to-short ratio is 1.64, still heavily skewed to the buy side. The long-to-short ratio across all names is skewed long: Bitcoin 1.21, Ethereum 1.45, and Dogecoin at 3.85. In the last twenty-three to twenty-four hours, Bitcoin saw 1,600 liquidations with shorts hit for $1.87 million against longs hit for $19.23 million, roughly a 10-to-1 ratio favoring the bears in the liquidation queue. Ethereum mirrors the pattern: shorts at $3.88 million, longs at $17.22 million. This is not balanced positioning; it is crowded bullish, and the day's selling is clearing leveraged longs.

Whale flows paint a picture of distribution into strength. Over the last twenty-four hours, Bitcoin saw a net $164.67 million flow onto exchanges, driven by $1.09 billion in inflows against $924.52 million in outflows. The three largest single moves onto exchanges were $184.98 million to Coinbase, and $158.71 million and $157.83 million to Kraken. The largest moves off exchanges were $158.19 million from Kraken and $149.24 million from Coinbase. The net direction is clear: whales are accumulating coins and moving them to trading venues. Over the past three weeks, this pattern has turned into a regime. Week ending August 15 saw $573 million move onto exchanges. Week ending August 22 saw $1,125 million move onto exchanges, the largest single week in the digest. Week ending August 29 (still in progress) shows $596 million onto exchanges. This is three consecutive weeks of net whale deposits to exchange wallets, a posture consistent with preparation for distribution or hedging into a rally. Bitcoin dominance holds steady at 59 percent, and the total market cap declined 4.41 percent on the day to $2.64 trillion.

Spot ETF flows offer a different signal. Bitcoin ETFs saw a net outflow of $201.9 million on August 28, a reversal from broader strength; over the last five sessions, Bitcoin ETFs recorded a net inflow of $924.5 million, but the single-day print is negative and same-direction days total only one. Ethereum ETFs, by contrast, show a net inflow of $102.1 million on the day, and over the last five sessions have netted $815.7 million inward, with same-direction days at ten, meaning Ethereum ETF flows have been consistently positive. Stablecoin float stands at $309.78 billion, up 1.11 percent over the past thirty days, a modest accumulation of dry powder. Bitcoin network fees are at 1 satoshi per byte, and difficulty is down 1.3 percent with 1,089 blocks until the next retarget, consistent with a period of lighter on-chain demand.

The read is a rally running into resistance after three weeks of accelerating appreciation, with leverage long and funding rates expensive, whales positioning to sell into the move via exchange deposit, and spot ETF capital showing a split signal (Bitcoin hesitant, Ethereum still bidding). A pullback inside an uptrend is normal, but the specific combination of overbought momentum, crowded long positioning, and three-week whale distribution onto exchanges warrants watching for a breakdown of the 200-day support or a failure to reclaim today's loss and hold Friday's lows.
